Feature Extraction a. Choose the feature (s) that represent each pixel ' s characteristics. For color images, these features could be RGB values or color spaces like LAB or HSV. For grayscale images, intensity values are commonly used. Cluster Initialization a. Decide on the number of clusters (K) you want to create. This choice depends on the specific image and application. b. Initialize K cluster centroids. These centroids represent the initial cluster centers, which can be randomly chosen or based on some heuristic. Clustering Algorithm (K-Means) a. b. c. d. Iterate through the following steps until convergence. Assignment Step: Assign each pixel to the nearest cluster centroid based on feature similarity (e.g. , Euclidean distance) . Update Step: Recalculate the cluster centroids as the mean of the pixels in each cluster. Convergence is reached when the cluster assignments no longer change significantly. Segmentation a. After convergence, the image is segmented based on the final cluster assignments. Each cluster represents a segment or region in the image. Post-processing a. Optionally, apply post-processing techniques to refine the segmentation, such as merging or splitting clusters based on specific criteria. FAST NUCES - Karachi Talha Shahid 13
